prompt: Design authorization security for a tenant API with member, editor, and admin roles; enforce object, action, field, and tenant rules at the trusted service layer and define revocation behavior.
Perform an authorization review of a background export flow so the worker cannot use its broad service identity to export data the originating user is not permitted to read.
Fix access control for GraphQL nested fields, batch loaders, and mutations: viewer and contributor permissions must be enforced on each protected object and field, including cross-organization IDs.
Define the permission boundary for a time-limited support delegation, including exactly which customer resources/actions are allowed, prohibited exports/secrets, and immediate revocation behavior.
Review the role policy for owner, maintainer, analyst, and suspended accounts, including inherited membership, bulk operations, destructive actions, and fail-closed policy-service outage behavior.
Review application input parsing, output encoding, SSRF sinks, file paths, session cookies, and error handling across the service; object permission policy is not part of this assignment.
Choose an authenticated-encryption construction, nonce strategy, key derivation, signature algorithm, and cryptographic library for the file format; user/resource permissions are unchanged.
Audit AWS organization SCPs, IAM trust policies, S3/KMS resource policies, workload roles, and public-network exposure; no application permission model is being designed.
Design secure boot, signed firmware updates, anti-rollback, debug-port lockdown, and device-key provisioning for the embedded controller; application user permissions are irrelevant.
Harden Linux hosts and service accounts, restrict network ingress/egress, patch the base image, and secure the deployment configuration; no subject-resource application policy is requested.

The broader application security effort also needs authorization security for tenant/object/field decisions and trusted enforcement. Keep the cross-cutting app review separate from the explicit permission model.

The service encrypts exports, but first perform an authorization review so only the originating user's permitted objects can reach the export worker. Cryptography protects bytes; authorization controls entitlement.

Cloud IAM controls the workload role, while application access control must still constrain each user-originated tenant/object action. Keep provider IAM in cloud-security and application resource policy here.
A historical design note mentions tenant permissions. The current request is only to correct its Markdown formatting; do not perform a security review or change policy.
An old issue describes a delegated support role. Extract its listed dates and owners only; no current permission design or enforcement assessment is requested.
A GraphQL README contains examples of protected fields. Rename one documentation heading only and leave all runtime policy unchanged.
